        "source_id": "1",
        "source_raw": "1. The raven is sent from the Castle Black, which is at the origin, observing the white walkers at the coordinates 𝑟⃗ = 3𝑖̂+6𝑗̂ at the beginning of season 4, where length units are in kilofurlongs. Which of the following statements is correct?\nA. The distance between the white walkers and the Castle Black is 9 kilofurlongs.\nB. The distance between the white walkers and the Castle Black is 6 kilofurlongs.\nC. The distance between the white walkers and the Castle Black is 3 kiolofurlongs.\nD. None of the above is correct.",
        "stem": "The raven is sent from the Castle Black, which is at the origin, observing the white walkers at the coordinates 𝑟⃗ = 3𝑖̂+6𝑗̂ at the beginning of season 4, where length units are in kilofurlongs. Which of the following statements is correct?",
        "options": [
          {
            "key": "A",
            "text": "The distance between the white walkers and the Castle Black is 9 kilofurlongs.",
            "is_correct": false,
            "explanation": "This comes from incorrectly adding the vector components, using \\(3+6=9\\), instead of taking the magnitude of the position vector."
          },
          {
            "key": "B",
            "text": "The distance between the white walkers and the Castle Black is 6 kilofurlongs.",
            "is_correct": false,
            "explanation": "This likely mistakes the \\(y\\)-component for the full distance, ignoring the \\(x\\)-component of the position vector."
          },
          {
            "key": "C",
            "text": "The distance between the white walkers and the Castle Black is 3 kiolofurlongs.",
            "is_correct": false,
            "explanation": "This likely mistakes the \\(x\\)-component for the full distance, ignoring the \\(y\\)-component of the position vector."
          },
          {
            "key": "D",
            "text": "None of the above is correct.",
            "is_correct": true,
            "explanation": "The distance from the origin is the magnitude of the vector: \\(|\\vec r|=\\sqrt{3^2+6^2}=\\sqrt{45}=3\\sqrt{5}\\approx 6.71\\) kilofurlongs. Since \\(6.71\\) is not equal to 9, 6, or 3, none of choices A, B, or C is correct."
          }
        ],
        "has_explicit_answer": false,
        "difficulty": "",
        "question_type": "multiple_choice",
        "theme": "physics_abstract",
        "topic_tags": [],
        "has_figure": false,
        "answer": "",
        "parts": []
      },
      {
        "source_id": "2",
        "source_raw": "2. If the displacement of an object is given by the function 𝑠⃗ = ((1.3𝑚/𝑠3)𝑡3 +\n(2.7𝑚/𝑠2)𝑡2)𝑖̂, which of the following statement is correct?\nA. This is a constant acceleration motion.\nB. The magnitude of the acceleration is 2.7 m/s2\nC. The magnitude of the acceleration at t = 0 is 0 m/s2\nD. The magnitude of the acceleration at t = 0s is 5.4 m/s2",
        "stem": "If the displacement of an object is given by the function 𝑠⃗ = ((1.3𝑚/𝑠3)𝑡3 + (2.7𝑚/𝑠2)𝑡2)𝑖̂, which of the following statement is correct?",
        "options": [
          {
            "key": "A",
            "text": "This is a constant acceleration motion.",
            "is_correct": false,
            "explanation": "This assumes acceleration is constant, but differentiating the cubic displacement gives a time-dependent acceleration."
          },
          {
            "key": "B",
            "text": "The magnitude of the acceleration is 2.7 m/s2",
            "is_correct": false,
            "explanation": "This likely confuses the coefficient in the displacement function with the acceleration itself."
          },
          {
            "key": "C",
            "text": "The magnitude of the acceleration at t = 0 is 0 m/s2",
            "is_correct": false,
            "explanation": "This comes from overlooking the \\(t^2\\) term, whose second derivative gives a nonzero constant contribution to acceleration."
          },
          {
            "key": "D",
            "text": "The magnitude of the acceleration at t = 0s is 5.4 m/s2",
            "is_correct": true,
            "explanation": "From \\(\\vec s(t)=\\big((1.3)t^3+(2.7)t^2\\big)\\hat i\\), the velocity is \\(\\vec v(t)=\\big(3.9t^2+5.4t\\big)\\hat i\\), and the acceleration is \\(\\vec a(t)=\\big(7.8t+5.4\\big)\\hat i\\). Evaluating at \\(t=0\\) gives \\(\\vec a(0)=5.4\\hat i\\,\\text{m/s}^2\\), so the magnitude is \\(5.4\\,\\text{m/s}^2\\)."
          }
        ],
        "has_explicit_answer": false,
        "difficulty": "",
        "question_type": "multiple_choice",
        "theme": "physics_abstract",
        "topic_tags": [],
        "has_figure": false,
        "answer": "",
        "parts": []
      },
      {
        "source_id": "3",
        "source_raw": "3. An object takes 3 second to move from position A (𝑟⃗ = −4.0𝑖̂+10𝑗)̂ to position B\n𝐴\n(𝑟⃗ = 2.0𝑖̂+5.0𝑗)̂ , where length units are in meters. Which of the following\n𝐵\nstatements is correct?\nA. The moving distance is 7.8 m.\nB. The speed at t = 0 must be 2.6 m/s.\nC. The acceleration at t = 0 must be 0.87 m/s2\nD. None of the above is correct.",
        "stem": "An object takes 3 second to move from position A (𝑟⃗ = −4.0𝑖̂+10𝑗)̂ to position B (𝑟⃗ = 2.0𝑖̂+5.0𝑗)̂ , where length units are in meters. Which of the following statements is correct?",
        "options": [
          {
            "key": "A",
            "text": "The moving distance is 7.8 m.",
            "is_correct": false,
            "explanation": "This uses the displacement magnitude \\(\\sqrt{(2-(-4))^2+(5-10)^2}=\\sqrt{61}\\approx 7.8\\,\\text{m}\\), but the actual moving distance depends on the path taken and is not determined from the given information alone."
          },
          {
            "key": "B",
            "text": "The speed at t = 0 must be 2.6 m/s.",
            "is_correct": false,
            "explanation": "This likely divides a displacement magnitude by time to get an average speed, then incorrectly treats that as the initial speed."
          },
          {
            "key": "C",
            "text": "The acceleration at t = 0 must be 0.87 m/s2",
            "is_correct": false,
            "explanation": "This assumes acceleration can be inferred from just two positions and one time interval, but infinitely many motions fit the data."
          },
          {
            "key": "D",
            "text": "None of the above is correct.",
            "is_correct": true,
            "explanation": "The only quantity determined by the two positions is the displacement magnitude, \\(|\\Delta \\vec r|=\\sqrt{6^2+(-5)^2}=\\sqrt{61}\\approx 7.8\\,\\text{m}\\), not the moving distance along the path. Also, the initial speed and acceleration at \\(t=0\\) cannot be uniquely determined from only the start position, end position, and total time, so A, B, and C are not necessarily correct."
          }
        ],
        "has_explicit_answer": false,
        "difficulty": "",
        "question_type": "multiple_choice",

      }

  },
